note: At the Battle of the Nile, Nelson caught the French fleet in Aboukir Bay, east of Alexandria, and destroyed it; the flagship L’Orient blew up, stranding Bonaparte’s army in Egypt.

event: A rebel earl captures the king of England
note: Simon de Montfort’s barons defeated and captured Henry III on the Downs above a Sussex town, and Montfort ruled England for a year.

event: Simon de Montfort is cut down
note: The future Edward I trapped Montfort in a loop of the River Avon in Worcestershire; the earl was killed and his body mutilated.

event: Swiss peasants ambush the Habsburg knights
note: Men of Schwyz rolled logs and stones down on an Austrian army strung out between a mountainside and a lake, securing the young Swiss Confederacy.

event: A Swiss hero gathers the enemy’s spears
note: The Swiss beat Duke Leopold III of Austria, who was killed; legend says Arnold Winkelried flung himself on the Austrian pikes to open a gap.

event: A prince wins his famous name
note: Prince Alexander of Novgorod surprised a Swedish force where the Izhora joins the Neva, and was called Nevsky ever after.

event: Ivan III outstares the Golden Horde
note: Russian and Tatar armies faced each other across a river south-west of Moscow for weeks until the khan withdrew, ending the Mongol yoke over Russia.
In fog on a ridge of hills in Thessaly, Roman legions broke Philip V’s Macedonian phalanx, showing the flexible legion could beat it.

event: Sparta wins the Peloponnesian War at a stroke
note: Lysander caught the Athenian fleet beached on the shore of the Dardanelles and captured almost all of it; Athens surrendered the next year.

event: Hannibal’s first great victory in Italy
note: On a snowy morning, Hannibal lured the Romans across an icy river in the Po valley and sprang an ambush from a hidden stream bed.

event: Frederick the Great routs the French in ninety minutes
note: Frederick’s cavalry, hidden behind a low hill in Saxony, crushed a French and imperial army twice the size of his own.
Russian and Austrian armies destroyed the Prussian army east of the Oder; Frederick wrote that all was lost.

event: Hawke chases the French fleet onto the rocks
note: In a gale, the British fleet followed the French into a rock-strewn bay on the coast of Brittany and destroyed them, ending a planned invasion of Britain.

event: The Dutch fleet is crushed in the North Sea
note: Admiral Duncan’s fleet broke the Dutch line off the coast of North Holland and captured eleven ships.

event: The bloodiest battle of the 18th century
note: Marlborough and Prince Eugene beat the French on the border of France and Belgium at the cost of some 20,000 allied casualties.
Peter the Great’s galleys outmanoeuvred becalmed Swedish warships off a peninsula on the Finnish coast.

event: “Forty thousand men defeated in forty minutes”
note: Wellington saw the French army stretched out on its march and struck it south of a Spanish university city, his greatest offensive victory.

event: Napoleon’s army escapes across a frozen river
note: Dutch engineers working in icy water built bridges in what is now Belarus; most of the remnant of the Grande Armée got across, but thousands of stragglers were left behind.

event: The first battle of the Crimean War
note: British and French troops stormed Russian positions on the heights above a river north of Sevastopol.

event: The Moors win Spain in a single battle
note: Tariq ibn Ziyad’s army killed the Visigothic king Roderic near a river in Andalusia, and within a few years almost all of Spain was under Muslim rule.

event: The last battle of the Hundred Years’ War
note: French cannon cut down the English attack on their fortified camp on the Dordogne; the English commander Talbot was killed and Gascony was lost.

event: A Scottish king is taken in battle
note: An English army defeated the Scots invading in support of France, just west of Durham, and captured King David II.

event: The last battle fought on English soil
note: The Duke of Monmouth’s rebels tried a night attack across the Somerset Levels and were routed; Judge Jeffreys’ Bloody Assizes followed.

event: Bonnie Prince Charlie’s Highlanders win in ten minutes
note: A dawn Highland charge east of Edinburgh scattered the government army of Sir John Cope.

event: The United Irishmen make their stand
note: British troops stormed the rebel camp on a hill above Enniscorthy in County Wexford, ending the rising in the south-east of Ireland.
Hetman Konstanty Ostrogski’s Polish–Lithuanian army beat a larger Russian army on the Dnieper in what is now Belarus.

event: Prince Eugene destroys an Ottoman army
note: Eugene of Savoy caught the Ottoman army half across a river in what is now Serbia, a defeat that pushed the Ottomans out of Hungary for good.

event: Stephen the Great’s victory in the fog
note: The prince of Moldavia lured a far larger Ottoman army into a misty marshy valley and routed it; the pope called him the Athlete of Christ.
The young Francis I of France beat the feared Swiss pikemen south-east of Milan in a two-day battle.
Italian and Allied troops crossed the Piave and broke the Austro-Hungarian army, which collapsed within days.

event: The first book printed in English
note: William Caxton printed his translation of tales of Troy while living in Bruges, before taking his press home to Westminster.
Prices of rare bulbs, some worth more than a house, collapsed at a sale in a tavern in the Dutch city of Haarlem.

event: Monks finish the Book of Kells
note: The richly decorated gospel book was probably begun on Iona and carried to the monastery of Kells in County Meath to keep it safe from Vikings.

event: The largest surviving medieval world map is drawn
note: The map, with Jerusalem at its centre and monsters at its edges, has hung for 700 years in a cathedral on the Welsh border.

event: The first public museum in Britain opens
note: Elias Ashmole gave his collection of curiosities to Oxford University, which built a museum for it in Broad Street.
The 70 m embroidery telling the story of 1066 was probably made in England for the cathedral of a Norman town, where it still hangs.

event: The oldest known cave paintings in France
note: Lions, rhinos and horses were painted in a cave above the Ardèche gorge; three cavers found it in December 1994.
Bison painted on the ceiling of a cave in Cantabria were first noticed in 1879 by an eight-year-old girl, María Sautuola.

event: A limestone figurine is carved in the Danube valley
note: The 11 cm Venus of Willendorf, found by railway workers in Lower Austria in 1908, is one of the oldest known images of the human body.

event: A silver cauldron is buried in a Danish bog
note: Peat cutters found the cauldron, decorated with gods and a figure with antlers, in a bog in Himmerland, Jutland, in 1891.

event: The Nebra sky disc is buried
note: A bronze disc inlaid with a gold sun, moon and stars, perhaps the oldest picture of the cosmos, was buried on a hilltop in Saxony-Anhalt.

event: Liu Bei’s army is burned in its camps
note: Lu Xun of Wu set fire to the long chain of Shu camps in the Yangtze gorges, and Liu Bei died the next year.
A Tang and Silla fleet destroyed a Japanese fleet sent to restore the kingdom of Baekje, at the mouth of a river in south-west Korea.

event: The largest naval battle of the Middle Ages
note: Zhu Yuanzhang, who later founded the Ming dynasty, used fireships to destroy Chen Youliang’s giant tower ships on China’s largest freshwater lake.
Nurhaci concentrated his forces to destroy four Ming columns one by one in the mountains east of Shenyang.
Western-style cannon on the walls of a Ming fortress town near the coast of Liaoning repelled Nurhaci, who died months later.

event: Russia and China fight over the Amur
note: Qing troops besieged the Cossack fort on the Amur river; the Treaty of Nerchinsk followed.
The emperor’s army crushed the Dzungar leader Galdan near the Tuul river, east of modern Ulaanbaatar.

event: A Sui invasion army drowns in a river
note: The Goguryeo general Eulji Mundeok let a huge Sui army cross a river in northern Korea, then attacked as it retreated; few of its 300,000 men got home.

event: Two warlords fight on the same plain five times
note: Takeda Shingen and Uesugi Kenshin clashed repeatedly where two rivers meet in Shinano province; in 1561 they are said to have fought hand to hand.
Takeda Shingen routed the young Ieyasu on a plateau north of Hamamatsu; Ieyasu had a portrait painted of his frightened face to remind himself.
Minamoto no Yoshitsune led horsemen down a steep slope behind a Taira fortress on the coast near modern Kobe.

event: A loyal samurai dies for the emperor
note: Kusunoki Masashige, ordered to fight a battle he knew he would lose, died with his brother on the shore near modern Kobe.
Saigō Takamori’s rebels besieged the conscript garrison in its great castle in Kyushu for 50 days without taking it.

event: Vietnam ambushes a Ming army in a mountain pass
note: Lê Lợi’s forces killed the Ming general Liu Sheng in an ambush in a pass north-east of Hanoi, ending twenty years of Chinese occupation.

event: The Tây Sơn ambush a Siamese fleet
note: Nguyễn Huệ lured the Siamese fleet into a stretch of the Mekong delta and destroyed it.
Kublai Khan’s cavalry beat the Burmese king’s elephants in the hills of Yunnan, a battle Marco Polo described.
King Naresuan of Ayutthaya killed the Burmese crown prince in single combat on war elephants, a story every Thai schoolchild knows.

event: A royal wedding becomes a massacre
note: Majapahit troops killed the king of Sunda and his party, who had come to marry his daughter to the Majapahit king, near the capital in East Java.

event: Muhammad of Ghor defeats Prithviraj Chauhan
note: The Ghurid victory north of Delhi opened northern India to the rule of the Delhi Sultanate.
Babur’s guns and mounted archers defeated Rana Sanga’s Rajput alliance west of Agra, securing the new Mughal Empire.

event: Aurangzeb defeats his brother for the throne
note: Dara Shikoh’s army broke when he climbed down from his elephant; Aurangzeb took Agra, imprisoned his father Shah Jahan and became emperor.

event: Britain wins the war for south India
note: Eyre Coote beat the French under Lally near a fort in the Carnatic, ending French hopes of an Indian empire.

event: The last battle of the first Anglo-Sikh war
note: British troops stormed the Sikh entrenchments on the Sutlej; thousands drowned when the bridge of boats behind them broke.

event: A desert post holds off a tank column
note: About 120 Indian soldiers held a border post in the Thar Desert overnight against Pakistani tanks until aircraft arrived at dawn.
Arab armies defeated the last great Persian army in the Zagros mountains, and the Sasanian empire never recovered.

event: A Roman emperor is taken prisoner
note: Shapur I captured Emperor Valerian and his army; Persian rock reliefs show Valerian kneeling before the shah.
The 16-year-old Baldwin IV of Jerusalem routed Saladin’s much larger army near Ramla.

event: The Ottomans destroy the Mamluk army
note: Selim I’s guns beat the Mamluk cavalry north of Aleppo; the old sultan Qansuh al-Ghawri died on the field and Syria passed to the Ottomans.

event: The charge of the Light Horse
note: Australian horsemen charged Ottoman trenches at dusk and took the town’s wells intact, breaking the Gaza–Beersheba line.

event: An Ottoman army freezes in the Caucasus
note: Enver Pasha’s winter offensive against the Russians in the mountains of north-east Anatolia lost most of his army to cold and hunger.

event: A governor’s greed brings the Mongols west
note: After its governor killed Genghis Khan’s merchants, the Mongols besieged the Khwarazmian frontier town on the Syr Darya, the start of their invasion of the Islamic world.

event: The Mongols’ first battle with the Rus’
note: Subutai and Jebe destroyed the armies of the Rus’ princes and the Cumans on the steppe north of the Sea of Azov, then rode away for fourteen years.

event: Bronze masks are buried in Sichuan
note: Pits found in 1986 near Chengdu held giant bronze heads with bulging eyes from a culture otherwise unknown to history.
Diviners at the last Shang capital carved questions on turtle shells and ox bones, the oldest known Chinese writing; the bones were found being sold as medicine in 1899.

event: Buddhist monks paint the caves of Ajanta
note: Thirty caves cut into a horseshoe gorge in Maharashtra hold some of the finest surviving ancient Indian paintings; a British hunting party rediscovered them in 1819.

event: The temples of Khajuraho are built
note: The Chandela kings built some 85 Hindu and Jain temples covered in carvings in central India; about 25 survive.

event: A temple is built as the sun god’s chariot
note: King Narasimhadeva I built the temple on the coast of Odisha as the chariot of the sun god, with 24 carved stone wheels.
The founder of the Persian Empire lies in a simple gabled stone tomb on a stepped plinth at his capital in the plain of Fars.

event: Darius carves his deeds on a cliff
note: The inscription in three languages, high on a cliff by the road from Babylon to Ecbatana, became the key to deciphering cuneiform.
The Hittite kings ruled from a walled city in central Anatolia, whose archives of clay tablets include one of the oldest known peace treaties.

event: Ethiopia beats Egypt in the highlands
note: Emperor Yohannes IV’s army destroyed an invading Egyptian force in what is now Eritrea, ending Egypt’s attempt to conquer Ethiopia.
Anglo-Egyptian troops broke into a fortified camp by the river where the Atbara joins the Nile, five months before Omdurman.

event: The Portuguese kill the king of Kongo
note: A Portuguese colonial army from Luanda defeated and beheaded King António I of Kongo, and the kingdom fell into civil war.

event: The Asante defeat a British governor
note: Asante troops overwhelmed Sir Charles MacCarthy’s force on the Gold Coast; his skull was kept as a trophy in Kumasi.

event: The last stand of the Shangani Patrol
note: Major Allan Wilson’s 34 men, chasing the Ndebele king Lobengula, were cut off by the flooded Shangani river and all killed.

event: British troops defeat the Boers north of the Orange
note: Sir Harry Smith beat Andries Pretorius’s Boers and annexed their land for six years.

event: The Boers besiege a British camp at a harbour
note: After the British were beaten off, Dick King rode 960 km in ten days to Grahamstown for help, raising the siege of Port Natal, now Durban.

event: A British column is driven off a mountain
note: Mounted troops attacking a Zulu stronghold in northern Zululand were caught by the main Zulu army; the next day the British won at Kambula.

event: An Italian outpost is overrun in the highlands
note: Ethiopian forces wiped out an Italian column on a mountain in Tigray, three months before Adwa.

event: Ethiopia and Portugal defeat the Adal Sultanate
note: Emperor Gelawdewos and the surviving Portuguese musketeers killed Imam Ahmad Gragn near Lake Tana, ending his conquest of Ethiopia.

event: The bloodiest battle of the East African campaign
note: Lettow-Vorbeck’s German force inflicted heavy losses on British and African troops in southern Tanzania before slipping away again.

event: A whole Italian army is cut off
note: A small British force raced across the desert of Cyrenaica to block the coast road and captured some 25,000 retreating Italians.
To keep it from Germany, the Royal Navy shelled the French fleet in its harbour near Oran, in Algeria, killing nearly 1,300 French sailors.
The Eighth Army outflanked the old French defences in southern Tunisia where Rommel’s army had dug in.
Justinian’s general crushed the Vandal king Gelimer west of Carthage, ending the Vandal kingdom.

event: The Arab conquest of North Africa begins
note: An Arab army killed the Byzantine governor Gregory at his capital in central Tunisia, whose Roman temples still stand.
The trading capital of the Ghana Empire, rich from Saharan gold and salt, lay in what is now south-east Mauritania, far from modern Ghana.

event: A Swahili town is abandoned to the forest
note: The coral-stone houses, palace and mosques of Gede, on the Kenyan coast near Malindi, were left to the forest in the 17th century.
The naturalistic heads cast at the sacred Yoruba city in Nigeria astonished Europeans when they were found in 1938.

event: A Black Watch square is broken
note: Beja warriors broke into a British square near the Red Sea coast of Sudan before being driven off; Kipling’s poem “Fuzzy-Wuzzy” honours them.

event: The first battle of the Mexican–American War
note: American artillery broke Mexican attacks on the prairie north of the Rio Grande, near modern Brownsville, Texas.
Taylor’s outnumbered army held a mountain pass south of Saltillo; the victory helped make him president.

event: A young engineer finds the way round
note: Captain Robert E. Lee scouted a path round Santa Anna’s position in the mountains on the road from Veracruz to Mexico City.
Union troops burned the Confederate supply train in a pass east of Santa Fe, ending the Confederate invasion of New Mexico.
Union troops beat a larger Confederate army, which included Cherokee regiments, in the Ozarks of north-west Arkansas.
Custer’s 7th Cavalry attacked Chief Black Kettle’s Cheyenne camp at dawn in western Oklahoma, killing him and many women and children.
Lakota and Cheyenne warriors fought Crook’s column to a standstill in southern Montana, eight days before the Little Bighorn.

event: The Nez Perce are attacked at dawn
note: Army troops surprised the fleeing Nez Perce camp in a Montana valley; the warriors pinned them down while the families escaped.

event: Geronimo surrenders for the last time
note: The Apache leader gave himself up to General Nelson Miles in Skeleton Canyon in the mountains of south-east Arizona.

event: Buffalo hunters hold off a war party
note: Twenty-eight hunters at a trading post in the Texas Panhandle beat off hundreds of Comanche and Cheyenne led by Quanah Parker.

event: French Canadians turn back an American invasion
note: Charles de Salaberry’s Voltigeurs and militia stopped an American army marching on Montreal at a ford on the Châteauguay River.
After Laura Secord walked 32 km to warn the British, Mohawk warriors ambushed an American column in the Niagara peninsula, and it surrendered.
Métis under Gabriel Dumont beat a force of police and volunteers in Saskatchewan.

event: Fur traders fight beside the Red River
note: North West Company Métis led by Cuthbert Grant killed the governor of the Hudson’s Bay Company’s settlement and twenty of his men.

event: Frontier militia destroy a Loyalist army
note: Frontiersmen from over the mountains surrounded Major Ferguson’s Loyalists on a ridge on the border of the Carolinas; Ferguson was killed.

event: A battle on the hottest day
note: Washington’s retrained army fought the British to a draw in New Jersey on a day so hot that men died of heatstroke; legend made “Molly Pitcher” its heroine.

event: Washington is outflanked in a creek valley
note: Howe’s army crossed upstream and turned Washington’s flank south-west of Philadelphia, which the British occupied two weeks later.
The Spanish and their Tlaxcalan allies killed thousands of unarmed people in the main square of a pilgrimage city beside the largest pyramid in the world.

event: A Maya town gives the Spanish twenty women, among them Malinche
note: After Cortés beat the Chontal Maya of Tabasco at Centla, they gave him women as tribute; one, Malinche, became his interpreter and adviser.

event: An indigenous rising in western Mexico
note: Caxcan warriors held out on fortified hills in Zacatecas and Jalisco; the viceroy himself led an army to crush them.

event: Gonzalo Pizarro wins by Lake Titicaca
note: In the civil wars among the conquistadors, Pizarro’s arquebusiers beat a royalist army near the shore of the lake.

event: The British Legion charges in a swamp
note: Bolívar’s army, with British volunteers, beat the royalists in the Andes north-east of Bogotá, two weeks before Boyacá.

event: Independence is won on a lake
note: Admiral Padilla’s squadron destroyed the last Spanish fleet in Venezuela on the lake, ending Spanish rule there.

event: Bolívar’s costly victory in the southern Andes
note: Bolívar attacked royalists dug in beside a ravine near Pasto in southern Colombia, opening the way to Quito.

event: A night attack scatters San Martín’s army
note: Royalists surprised the patriot camp at night near Talca in central Chile; San Martín regrouped and won at Maipú two weeks later.
A Chilean army beat Santa Cruz’s confederation in an Andean valley of Peru; Chile still celebrates it in a famous song.
Brazilian cavalry caught Francisco Solano López with his last followers in the hills of northern Paraguay; he died saying “I die with my country.”

event: The river fortress of Paraguay falls
note: Brazilian ironclads forced their way past the batteries guarding the Paraguay river, and the fortress fell after a long siege.

event: The first battle of the Chaco War
note: Paraguayan troops besieged a Bolivian fort in the dry scrub of the Gran Chaco for three weeks until thirst forced it to surrender.

event: The Haitians hold a small fort
note: Toussaint’s officer Dessalines held a fort above the Artibonite valley against Napoleon’s army for three weeks, then broke out.

event: A temple with a labyrinth of stone galleries
note: The Chavín built a temple high in the Peruvian Andes, with a carved stone idol, the Lanzón, at the heart of its dark passages.

event: A walled city on a mountain ridge
note: The Chachapoyas people walled a ridge in northern Peru with stone up to 19 m high, around hundreds of round houses.
Deep in the forest of northern Guatemala, the Preclassic Maya built La Danta, one of the largest pyramids in the world by volume.

event: The British storm a Waikato pā
note: After failed assaults on the defensive line between the Waikato River and a lake, the Māori defenders raised a white flag to talk and were taken prisoner.

event: Australians hold an airstrip in the highlands
note: Reinforcements flown in under fire held the gold-mining town’s airstrip in New Guinea against a Japanese attack.

event: Marines hold a ridge above the airfield
note: US Marine Raiders beat off Japanese night attacks on the ridge south of Henderson Field on Guadalcanal.
American forces took the world’s largest atoll lagoon from the Japanese in four days.
American carrier pilots shot down some 600 Japanese aircraft west of the Marianas, destroying Japan’s naval air power.
Allied landings by the bays of Hollandia, now Jayapura in Indonesia, cut off 40,000 Japanese troops further east.

event: The waters of Maui run red
note: Kamehameha’s army, with cannon handled by two foreign sailors, beat the Maui forces in the ʻĪao Valley; the dead are said to have dammed the stream.

event: Marines land on a small island harbour
note: On the first day of the Guadalcanal campaign, US Marines took the small islands across the sound where Japan had a seaplane base.

event: Lapita potters reach the far Pacific
note: The people who first settled the remote Pacific islands made distinctive stamped pottery, named after a site in New Caledonia.

event: A trilithon is raised in Tonga
note: The Tongan king Tuʻitātui built the great stone gateway, two uprights and a lintel of coral limestone, on the island of Tongatapu.

event: Epaminondas’s oblique attack breaks the Spartans
note: The Thebans massed their left wing 50 ranks deep and shattered the Spartan army at Leuctra in Boeotia, ending Sparta’s dominance of Greece; the battle trophy’s base survives.

event: Rome defeats the Macedonian phalanx at Pydna
note: The legions of Lucius Aemilius Paullus broke King Perseus’s phalanx on uneven ground near Pydna, below Mount Olympus, ending the Macedonian kingdom.

event: Scipio starves out the Celtiberians of Numantia
note: Scipio Aemilianus ringed the hill town with 9 km of walls and starved it out after twenty years of resistance; many defenders chose death over surrender. Its ruins lie near Soria.

event: Pelagius defeats the Umayyads at Covadonga
note: A small Asturian force under Pelagius (Pelayo) beat an Umayyad detachment in a valley of the Picos de Europa, traditionally the beginning of the Christian Reconquista.
Basques ambushed the rearguard of Charlemagne’s army in a pass in the western Pyrenees, killing Roland, whose death became the subject of the Song of Roland.

event: Flemish militias defeat the French knights
note: The town militias of Flanders routed the French chivalry by a stream outside Kortrijk (Courtrai) and hung hundreds of captured golden spurs in a church.
John I of Portugal and his English archers defeated a much larger Castilian army near Aljubarrota, securing Portugal’s independence; the monastery of Batalha was built in thanks.

event: James IV of Scotland is killed at Flodden
note: James IV, invading England in support of France, was killed with much of his nobility by an English army at Branxton in Northumberland: the last British monarch to die in battle.

event: The Andean rebel Túpac Amaru II is executed
note: After leading the largest rising against Spanish rule in the Andes, José Gabriel Condorcanqui was executed, with his wife Micaela Bastidas, in the main square of Cusco, the old Inca capital.

event: Edward Jenner gives the first vaccination
note: Country doctor Edward Jenner inoculated eight-year-old James Phipps with cowpox at Berkeley in Gloucestershire, then showed that the boy was immune to smallpox.

event: Tycho Brahe builds his observatory, Uraniborg
note: Granted the island of Hven in the Øresund by King Frederick II of Denmark, Tycho built the most advanced observatory in pre-telescope Europe there.

event: Three leaders sign the accords dissolving the USSR
note: The leaders of Russia, Ukraine and Belarus met at a government hunting lodge at Viskuli in the Białowieża Forest, by the Polish border, and declared that the Soviet Union had ceased to exist.

event: Thutmose III defeats the Canaanite kings
note: The pharaoh surprised a Canaanite coalition by marching through a narrow pass to the city of Megiddo, then besieged it for seven months: the first battle recorded in detail. Megiddo gave its name to Armageddon.

event: Shalmaneser III fights a coalition including King Ahab
note: The Assyrian king fought twelve allied kings, among them Ahab of Israel, at Qarqar on the Orontes in north-west Syria, probably Tell Qarqur; his inscription is the first record of camels in battle.
Qin defeated the state of Zhao near modern Gaoping in Shanxi after a long stand-off and reportedly buried the surrendered Zhao army alive, clearing its path to unify China.

event: Maharana Pratap fights the Mughals at Haldighati
note: The ruler of Mewar fought Akbar’s army under Man Singh in a narrow pass in the Aravalli hills, north of Udaipur; though he lost the field, he became a hero of Rajput resistance.

event: Arthur Wellesley defeats the Marathas at Assaye
note: The future Duke of Wellington beat a far larger Maratha army where two rivers meet in the Deccan, north-east of Aurangabad; he later called it the best thing he ever did in the fighting way.
A small British and Indian garrison held the fort of Chitral, deep in the Hindu Kush, for about seven weeks until relief columns fought their way over the mountain passes.

event: Nobunaga’s musketeers break the Takeda cavalry
note: Oda Nobunaga’s arquebusiers, firing from behind wooden palisades, cut down the famous Takeda horsemen on the plain of Shitaragahara near Nagashino Castle.

event: The Minamoto destroy the Taira fleet
note: The Minamoto clan defeated the Taira at sea in the narrow Kanmon Strait between Honshu and Kyushu; the child emperor Antoku drowned, and the Kamakura shogunate followed.

event: Tran Hung Dao traps a Mongol fleet on stakes
note: The Vietnamese general lured a Yuan Mongol fleet over iron-tipped stakes driven into the Bach Dang estuary near Ha Long Bay; as the tide fell, the ships were impaled and destroyed.

event: Zhukov defeats Japan on the Mongolian border
note: Soviet and Mongolian forces under Georgy Zhukov encircled the Japanese army on the Khalkhin Gol river on the Manchurian border; Japan then turned its ambitions south.

event: The first skull of ‘Peking Man’ is found
note: Pei Wenzhong found a Homo erectus skullcap in a limestone cave at Zhoukoudian, about 50 km south-west of Beijing; most of the fossils vanished in 1941.

event: Russia and Qing China sign their first treaty
note: Envoys met at the Russian fort of Nerchinsk in eastern Siberia and fixed the border along the Argun river and the Stanovoy mountains, with Jesuit priests interpreting in Latin.
After a night march across the desert, Wolseley’s army stormed Urabi Pasha’s trenches at Tel el-Kebir, between Cairo and the Suez Canal, beginning Britain’s long occupation of Egypt.
Boer commandos scaled the steep hill on the Natal border and routed the British force on its summit, winning the First Boer War.

event: Ras Alula destroys an Italian column
note: Ethiopian troops destroyed an Italian column marching to relieve a fort inland from Massawa, on the Red Sea coast of what is now Eritrea.

event: The golden rhinoceros is buried at Mapungubwe
note: Mapungubwe, by the meeting of the Limpopo and Shashe rivers, was the capital of southern Africa’s first great kingdom; a gold-foil rhinoceros from a royal grave on its hill was found in 1933.

event: The Battle of the Three Kings
note: King Sebastian of Portugal’s crusade into Morocco ended in disaster by the Loukkos river near Ksar el-Kebir; he and both rival Moroccan sultans died, and Portugal soon fell to Spain.

event: Farmers find the Gnostic Gospels in Upper Egypt
note: A farmer digging for fertiliser below the Jabal al-Tarif cliffs near Nag Hammadi found a jar holding thirteen leather-bound codices, including the Gospel of Thomas.

event: Andrew Jackson crushes the Red Stick Creeks
note: Jackson’s army, with Cherokee and Lower Creek allies, stormed the Red Sticks’ fortified bend of the Tallapoosa River in Alabama, ending the Creek War.

event: Paraguay repels the Triple Alliance at Curupayty
note: Paraguayan troops behind a trench line by the Paraguay River cut down an assault by Brazil and Argentina, the Allies’ worst defeat of the War of the Triple Alliance.
Jean-Jacques Dessalines’s army took the French forts ringing Cap-Français, forcing Rochambeau to evacuate; Haiti declared independence six weeks later.
After a 1,900 km fighting retreat, Chief Joseph of the Nez Perce surrendered in the Bear Paw Mountains of Montana, about 65 km from the Canadian border: ‘I will fight no more forever.’

event: Isaac Brock dies repelling an American invasion
note: British regulars, Canadian militia and Mohawk warriors threw back an American invasion across the Niagara River; General Isaac Brock was killed leading a charge up Queenston Heights.

Colorado volunteers under John Chivington attacked a peaceful Cheyenne and Arapaho camp on Sand Creek in eastern Colorado, killing well over a hundred people, most of them women, children and the elderly.

event: Australians defeat a Japanese landing at Milne Bay
note: Australian troops beat off a Japanese landing at the head of Milne Bay, on the eastern tip of New Guinea: the first time Japanese forces were decisively defeated on land in the war.
US Marines and soldiers spent ten weeks taking a small coral island in Palau from Japanese defenders dug into limestone caves, one of the costliest battles of the Pacific war.

event: Shackleton’s Endurance sinks in the ice
note: Crushed by pack ice in the Weddell Sea, Shackleton’s ship sank off Antarctica; all 28 men survived after an epic journey. The wreck was found in 2022, 3,000 m down.
Sponge divers off the small Greek island of Antikythera, between Crete and the Peloponnese, raised objects from a Roman-era wreck, among them a corroded geared astronomical calculator.

event: Epaminondas dies in his moment of victory
note: The Theban general broke the Spartan line once more in Arcadia but was mortally wounded, and Theban power died with him.

event: The Greeks burn the Persian fleet ashore
note: On the same day as Plataea, tradition says, a Greek force landed on the Ionian coast opposite Samos and destroyed the beached Persian ships.
Two quarrelling Roman commanders were destroyed separately by the Cimbri and Teutones by the Rhône, at what is now Orange.
Gaius Marius ambushed the migrating Germanic tribe below Mont Sainte-Victoire in Provence.
A year after the Teutones, the Cimbri were annihilated on a plain in Piedmont, ending the threat to Italy.
The young Caesar Julian beat a much larger Alamannic army by the Rhine and captured their king, Chnodomar.

event: A wind decides the last battle of the old gods
note: Theodosius I beat the pagan-backed usurper Eugenius in a valley in what is now Slovenia, helped by a fierce bora wind blowing into the enemy’s faces.

event: Clovis drives the Visigoths from Gaul
note: The Frankish king killed the Visigothic king Alaric II in battle north-west of Poitiers and took south-west Gaul.
King Bridei’s Picts killed King Ecgfrith of Northumbria by a loch in Angus, ending Northumbrian power north of the Forth.
Emerging from hiding in the Somerset marshes, Alfred defeated the Danes in Wiltshire; Guthrum was baptised and Wessex survived.

event: Harald Hardrada’s first victory in England
note: The Norwegian king beat the northern earls south of York, five days before he was killed at Stamford Bridge.

event: A king captures his own brother
note: Henry I of England defeated and imprisoned his elder brother Robert, Duke of Normandy, for the rest of his long life.
William Marshal, aged about 70, beat the rebel barons and their French allies in the streets of the city, saving the throne for the boy Henry III.
A Scottish raiding army beat the English under Harry Hotspur in Northumberland, though its leader the Earl of Douglas was killed.
Henry IV beat the Percy rebels north of the town; the young future Henry V was wounded in the face by an arrow.

event: The first battle of the Wars of the Roses
note: The Duke of York’s men fought through the streets of a Hertfordshire market town and captured the king, Henry VI.

event: The last battle of the Wars of the Roses
note: Henry VII beat the rebels backing the pretender Lambert Simnel near Newark; the boy was put to work in the royal kitchens.

event: A Scottish army is routed in a bog
note: A small English force scattered a larger Scottish army on the border; James V died three weeks later, leaving the baby Mary as queen.

event: Mary, Queen of Scots, loses her last battle
note: After escaping from Lochleven Castle, Mary’s army was beaten in 45 minutes on the south side of Glasgow, and she fled to England.

event: A Jacobite battle both sides claimed to have lost
note: Each army’s right wing routed the other’s left on a moor above Dunblane; the Jacobite rising faded away soon after.

event: Spanish soldiers fight in the Highlands
note: A small Jacobite force with 250 Spanish marines was driven out of a glen in Wester Ross by government troops.

event: The bloodiest battle in Irish history
note: William III’s army beat the Jacobites in County Galway after their French commander, St Ruth, was decapitated by a cannonball.
Irish forces destroyed an English army marching to relieve a fort on the Blackwater, near Armagh.

event: The Black Prince fights in Castile
note: English archers beat a Castilian and French army in La Rioja, briefly restoring Peter the Cruel to his throne.

event: Ferdinand and Isabella secure their crown
note: A battle by the Douro against the Portuguese king, who claimed Castile for his wife, ended indecisively but left Isabella’s claim secure.
Caliph Yaqub al-Mansur routed Alfonso VIII near Ciudad Real; the defeat was avenged at Las Navas de Tolosa seventeen years later.

event: A young Dante fights in the cavalry
note: Guelph Florence beat Ghibelline Arezzo in the upper Arno valley; Dante Alighieri, aged 24, rode in the front line.

event: Charles of Anjou wins the Kingdom of Sicily
note: King Manfred, the last Hohenstaufen ruler of southern Italy, was killed fighting the French prince backed by the pope.

event: Austria beats a larger Italian army
note: Archduke Albrecht’s outnumbered army beat the Italians in the hills between Verona and the Mincio, though Austria still had to give up Venetia.

event: The Ottomans destroy a Serbian army
note: A small Ottoman force surprised the Serbian army in its camp by the river in Thrace at night; both Serbian kings were killed.

event: An Ottoman grand vizier dies on the Danube
note: Louis of Baden beat the Ottomans at a bend of the Danube in what is now Serbia; the grand vizier Köprülü Fazıl Mustafa Pasha was killed.

event: Jan Sobieski storms an Ottoman camp
note: The Polish hetman, a year before he became king, attacked the Ottoman camp beside a great fortress on the Dniester at dawn after a freezing night.

event: Rumyantsev routs a vast Ottoman army
note: A Russian army outnumbered several times over beat the grand vizier near a lake in what is now southern Moldova.
The farmers of Dithmarschen opened the sluices on the marsh and destroyed the Danish king’s army and its Black Guard of mercenaries.

event: A city wins freedom from its archbishop
note: The citizens of Cologne and their allies defeated their archbishop’s army in one of the largest battles of medieval Europe.
The Great Elector’s cavalry defeated a Swedish army north-west of Berlin, the first victory of what became Prussia.
Field Marshal Daun beat the Prussians in central Bohemia, and Frederick had to lift the siege of Prague.

event: Norse chess pieces are buried on a Hebridean island
note: Some 93 pieces carved from walrus ivory, with glum kings and shield-biting berserkers, were found in a sandbank on the Isle of Lewis in 1831.

event: Two women are buried in a Viking ship
note: The richly carved ship, with a cart, sledges and animals, was buried in a mound near the Oslofjord and dug up in 1904.

event: A man is laid in a bog with a noose round his neck
note: The body, so well preserved by the peat in central Jutland that its finders in 1950 thought it a recent murder, was probably a sacrifice.
General Gyebaek and 5,000 men fought a Silla army ten times their size in central Korea; the kingdom of Baekje fell days later.
General Gang Gam-chan defeated the Liao invaders in north-west Korea; few of the 100,000 Khitan soldiers got home.

event: Korea’s navy is destroyed without Admiral Yi
note: With Yi Sun-sin in disgrace, his replacement led the Korean fleet into a Japanese trap near Geoje island and lost almost every ship.

event: Japan’s new navy beats China’s Beiyang Fleet
note: The largest naval battle of the age of steam before Tsushima was fought off the mouth of the river on the Korean border.
Japanese troops took the forts of the naval base on the Shandong coast and its torpedo boats attacked the fleet; Admiral Ding Ruchang killed himself.
Eleven days after Nobunaga’s death, Toyotomi Hideyoshi beat the traitor Akechi Mitsuhide between a mountain and the river south-west of Kyoto.
Hideyoshi beat Shibata Katsuie by a lake north of Lake Biwa; seven young samurai who distinguished themselves became famous.

event: The last clan to defy Hideyoshi surrenders
note: Hideyoshi’s huge army besieged the Hōjō clan’s castle for three months, holding feasts and tea ceremonies outside the walls.

event: An archer shoots a fan from a boat
note: In the Genpei War, Nasu no Yoichi hit a fan set on the mast of a Taira boat off a plateau on Shikoku; the Minamoto drove the Taira out to sea.

event: Conscripts fight samurai in the rain
note: For seventeen days the new imperial army fought Saigō Takamori’s rebels for a hill road north of Kumamoto; whoever held it controlled the way to the castle.
Samurai from southern Japan took Shuri Castle on Okinawa, and the island kingdom paid tribute to Japan and China alike for 270 years.

event: Li Shimin wins two wars in one battle
note: The future Emperor Taizong of Tang beat a relief army at a pass on the Yellow River, and both rival warlords surrendered.
The Song official Yu Yunwen rallied troops at a ferry crossing on the Yangtze and beat the Jin emperor’s attempt to cross.

event: A Mongol Great Khan dies besieging a fortress
note: Möngke Khan died outside a Song cliff fortress in Sichuan, and the Mongol armies in the Middle East turned back for the succession.

event: The Cham kings’ holy valley of temples
note: For nearly a thousand years the kings of Champa built red-brick tower temples to Shiva in a jungle valley in central Vietnam.

event: A Mekong port trades with Rome
note: Excavations at the port of the kingdom of Funan, in southern Vietnam, found Roman coins, Indian seals and Chinese mirrors.
A stone found by a river near Palembang in Sumatra tells of a king’s holy journey with an army of 20,000 that founded the maritime empire.

event: An inscription in a new Thai script
note: The stone, said to record King Ram Khamhaeng of Sukhothai, describes a kingdom where “there are fish in the water and rice in the fields”.
The Afghan leader surprised the Mughal camp by the Ganges at dawn; Humayun escaped across the river with the help of a water-carrier.
Sher Shah Suri beat the Mughals again by the Ganges, and Humayun spent fifteen years in exile before he won back his throne.
An East India Company army beat the ruler of Mysore on the Coromandel coast, saving Madras.

event: Lord Lake breaks the Maratha army of the north
note: The British beat the European-trained battalions of Daulat Rao Scindia south-west of Delhi, in one of the hardest fights of the Second Anglo-Maratha War.

event: A two-day battle in the Punjab
note: British troops stormed the Sikh entrenchments and nearly lost before the Sikh army withdrew, in the First Anglo-Sikh War.
A British artillery bombardment broke the last Sikh army in the Punjab, which Britain annexed weeks later.

event: The Kandyans destroy a Portuguese army
note: King Vimaladharmasuriya I trapped the Portuguese in the hill country of central Sri Lanka, keeping the Kandyan kingdom independent.
About 600 Gurkhas held a small fort near Dehradun against British assaults for a month; the British later recruited Gurkhas into their own army.
Mahmud Hotak’s Afghans beat a much larger Persian army outside Isfahan and then starved the capital into surrender.
The last Umayyad caliph, Marwan II, was beaten by a tributary of the Tigris in northern Iraq and killed months later in Egypt.

event: Muhammad’s followers are beaten below a mountain
note: A Meccan army defeated the Muslims at the foot of a mountain north of Medina after archers left their post to seize booty.

event: The Arabs’ first great victory over Byzantium
note: Khalid ibn al-Walid’s army beat the Byzantines in southern Palestine, opening the way to the conquest of Syria.
Turkish armies beat the crusader states near an ancient city in what is now south-east Turkey and captured Count Baldwin of Edessa.

event: A Byzantine emperor is ambushed in a pass
note: The Seljuks ambushed Manuel I Komnenos’s army in a mountain pass in Anatolia; he compared it to Manzikert.

event: The Mongols defeat the Seljuks of Rum
note: A Mongol army broke the Seljuk sultanate of Anatolia, which became a Mongol vassal.

event: An Egyptian army beats the Ottomans
note: Ibrahim Pasha, son of Muhammad Ali of Egypt, defeated the Ottomans near the Euphrates; the young officer Helmuth von Moltke advised the losing side.
Vartan Mamikonian’s Armenians lost to the Sasanian Persians but won the right to stay Christian; the Armenian Church honours him as a saint.

event: Alexander fights the Scythians at the edge of the world
note: Alexander crossed the river now called the Syr Darya and beat the nomad horse archers, near the city he founded as Alexandria Eschate.

event: A Khwarazmian prince beats a Mongol army
note: Jalal ad-Din Mingburnu defeated a Mongol force north of Kabul, one of the very few Mongol defeats of Genghis Khan’s wars.

event: A prince leaps his horse into a river to escape Genghis Khan
note: Cornered on the bank of the Indus, Jalal ad-Din rode his horse off a cliff into the river and swam to safety; Genghis Khan is said to have admired him.

event: Belisarius defeats the Vandals at the tenth milestone
note: Justinian’s general beat the Vandal army ten Roman miles from Carthage and marched into the city two days later.

event: Caesar is nearly beaten in Africa
note: Surrounded by Numidian cavalry near the coast of what is now Tunisia, Caesar’s small force barely fought its way back to camp.
Leopoldo O’Donnell’s army defeated the Moroccans and entered the city near the Mediterranean coast, the high point of the Hispano-Moroccan War.

event: The last battle fought in red coats
note: Anglo-Egyptian troops beat a Mahdist army on the Nile in northern Sudan; it is said to be the last time British soldiers fought in scarlet.

event: British troops beat Osman Digna near the Red Sea
note: A British force landed at Suakin defeated the Beja followers of the Mahdi, avenging an Egyptian defeat on the same ground weeks earlier.

event: A Mahdist invasion of Egypt is stopped
note: Anglo-Egyptian troops destroyed a Mahdist army marching down the Nile into Egypt; its commander Wad al-Nujumi was killed.
Italian forces beat Ras Mengesha’s army in what is now Eritrea, encouraging the invasion that ended at Adwa.

event: The father of a deposed emperor is defeated
note: Government forces beat Negus Mikael, father of the deposed emperor Lij Iyasu, north of Addis Ababa, securing the regency of Ras Tafari, later Haile Selassie.

event: Shewa wins the south of Ethiopia
note: Menelik of Shewa defeated the king of Gojjam and won control of the rich lands of the south-west.

event: An Ethiopian emperor dies fighting the Mahdists
note: Emperor Yohannes IV was shot as his army was winning on the Sudanese border; his army broke up when news of his death spread.

event: The turning point of the Zulu War
note: Evelyn Wood’s fortified camp in northern Zululand beat off the main Zulu army, the day after the British disaster at Hlobane.

event: A British column marches to relieve Eshowe
note: Lord Chelmsford’s square beat off a Zulu attack in the coastal plain of Zululand and went on to relieve the besieged mission at Eshowe.
The future king destroyed his brother Mbuyazi’s faction on the banks of the Tugela river; thousands died.

event: The Asante are defeated near the coast
note: British, Danish and Ga forces beat an Asante army on the plains north of Accra.

event: Someone engraves a piece of ochre
note: Crosshatched patterns on ochre and shell beads from a cave above the sea on South Africa’s southern coast are among the oldest known signs of symbolic thought.

event: Animals are painted on slabs of stone
note: Painted stones from a cave in the Huns Mountains of southern Namibia, named for the Moon landing of the week they were found, are among Africa’s oldest art.

event: Rock painters record a green Sahara
note: Thousands of paintings on a sandstone plateau in south-east Algeria show cattle, hunters and dancers from when the desert was grassland.

event: Terracotta heads are fired in central Nigeria
note: The Nok culture made life-size clay sculptures with pierced eyes and was among the first in West Africa to smelt iron.

event: One of the oldest cities south of the Sahara
note: A trading town grew up on the inland delta of the Niger without walls or palaces; it was abandoned around 1400 for nearby Djenné.

event: A mud-brick temple towers over Nubia
note: The capital of the Kingdom of Kush by the third cataract of the Nile was dominated by a great temple, the Western Deffufa.

event: Farmers terrace the foot of the Rift Valley wall
note: Stone-walled terraces and irrigation channels cover the escarpment in northern Tanzania, built by farmers who left around 1700.

event: A stone-walled hilltop town in the far north
note: The town in today’s Kruger National Park, linked to the trade of Great Zimbabwe, held a king and queen buried with gold.
French and Native warriors destroyed a British army near the forks of the Ohio; Braddock was killed and his aide George Washington had two horses shot under him.
Washington’s Virginians gave up their makeshift stockade in the Pennsylvania mountains to the French, opening the French and Indian War.
Loyalists and Mohawk and Seneca warriors ambushed a militia column in the Mohawk Valley; neighbours and kin fought each other.

event: New England militia beat Burgoyne’s raiders
note: John Stark’s militia destroyed a German detachment sent to seize supplies, weakening Burgoyne before Saratoga.

event: Cornwallis wins a battle and loses a campaign
note: Nathanael Greene’s army retreated from the courthouse in North Carolina, but Cornwallis lost a quarter of his men and marched off to Yorktown.

event: Daniel Boone’s son dies in an ambush
note: Kentucky militia rushed across the Licking River into an ambush by Native warriors and Loyalists, almost a year after Yorktown.

event: The worst defeat of the US Army by Native Americans
note: Little Turtle and Blue Jacket’s warriors overran Arthur St. Clair’s camp on the upper Wabash in Ohio; nearly 1,000 Americans died.
British and Native forces beat an American army on the River Raisin in Michigan; wounded prisoners were killed the next day.
Winfield Scott’s grey-uniformed brigade beat the British in Upper Canada; West Point cadets still wear grey in its honour, it is said.

event: A lake battle ends a British invasion
note: American ships anchored in a bay on Lake Champlain beat the British squadron, and the invading army turned back to Canada.
British and Canadian troops beat a larger American army on a farm by the St Lawrence, ending the threat to Montreal.

event: A night attack on an American camp
note: A small British force surprised the American camp at the head of Lake Ontario and captured both its generals.

event: Black Hawk’s band is trapped by a river
note: Soldiers and a steamboat attacked the Sauk and Meskwaki trying to cross the Mississippi in Wisconsin, ending the Black Hawk War.

event: The army destroys a hidden canyon camp
note: Ranald Mackenzie’s cavalry burned the Comanche, Kiowa and Cheyenne villages in a Texas canyon and killed over 1,000 of their horses.

event: Scouts hold a sandbar for nine days
note: Fifty frontier scouts dug in on an island in a dry river in Colorado against Cheyenne and Lakota warriors until relief arrived.

event: Poundmaker’s Cree beat a Canadian column
note: Cree and Assiniboine warriors beat an attack on their camp in Saskatchewan; Chief Poundmaker let the soldiers retreat.
A 400 m effigy of a snake with a coiled tail lies on a ridge in southern Ohio; its builders and date are still argued over.

event: Huge earthen rings in the Mississippi valley
note: Hunter-gatherers built concentric ridges and great mounds in north-east Louisiana, centuries before farming reached the region.

event: Peru’s last stand in the War of the Pacific
note: Andrés Cáceres’s guerrilla army was destroyed by the Chileans in the northern Andes, and Peru made peace three months later.

event: Peru’s last victory of the War of the Pacific
note: Peruvian troops beat a Chilean force in a ravine of the Atacama, but had to retreat and abandon the province.

event: The largest battle of the Cisplatine War
note: Argentine and Uruguayan forces beat the Brazilian army near the border, helping to make Uruguay independent.
José Gervasio Artigas beat the Spanish royalists north of Montevideo and spared his prisoners.
Antonio José de Sucre defeated an invading Peruvian army south of Cuenca in what is now Ecuador.

event: Children fight in Paraguay’s last battles
note: About 3,500 Paraguayans, most of them boys with painted-on moustaches, faced 20,000 Brazilians; Paraguay keeps the date as Children’s Day.
Poorly armed backlanders of Piauí and Ceará fought the Portuguese by a river in north-east Brazil; they lost, but the Portuguese army withdrew.
Máximo Gómez and Antonio Maceo’s mambises routed a Spanish column in central Cuba during their invasion of the west.

event: Baymen beat off a Spanish fleet
note: Settlers, enslaved men and a British sloop drove off a Spanish attack on a small island off the coast of what is now Belize.

event: Morelos holds out in a besieged town
note: José María Morelos’s insurgents held a town in Morelos against a royalist army for 72 days, then broke out.

event: Hidalgo’s army wins in the mountains
note: Miguel Hidalgo’s insurgent horde beat the royalists in a pass west of Mexico City, but he turned back rather than attack the capital.

event: A Moche lord is buried in gold
note: The untouched tomb of a Moche ruler, found in 1987 in a mud-brick pyramid in northern Peru, held gold, silver and the bodies of his attendants.

event: A solar observatory of thirteen towers
note: A row of towers on a ridge in the coastal desert of Peru marked the sunrise through the year, perhaps the oldest solar observatory in the Americas.

event: An ash fall buries a Maya village
note: A volcanic eruption sealed a farming village in El Salvador so quickly that dinners, gardens and sleeping mats were preserved.

event: The Olmecs carve their colossal heads
note: The first great Olmec centre, on a plateau in Veracruz, left basalt heads weighing up to 25 tonnes, carved from stone dragged from distant mountains.

event: An Olmec ceremonial centre rises in the swamps
note: The Olmecs built a clay pyramid and buried mosaic pavements of serpentine on an island in the Tabasco wetlands.

event: A Māori pā defeats a British assault
note: Hone Heke and Kawiti’s men, in a pā built to withstand cannon, cut down a frontal attack in Northland.

event: A dawn attack on a farm stockade
note: Māori warriors attacked the British post in the Hutt Valley north of Wellington; a bugler was killed still sounding the alarm.

event: A knife-edge ridge in New Guinea
note: Australian troops fought along a narrow ridge in the Finisterre Range to drive the Japanese from their positions above the Ramu valley.
Australian infantry and tanks fought up the slopes to a German Lutheran mission above Finschhafen in New Guinea.

event: An atoll falls in a week
note: American troops took the islands of the atoll in the Marshalls; it later became a nuclear test site.
Carlson’s Raiders landed from submarines on Butaritari in the Gilberts; nine men left behind were later executed.

event: The oldest known burials in Australia
note: A woman was cremated and a man buried sprinkled with ochre beside a now-dry lake in New South Wales.

event: The great marae of Polynesian voyagers
note: The sacred stone platform on Raiatea was the centre of a voyaging network across the eastern Pacific; navigators carried its stones to new islands.
